Core validation passed

Core Radiology, Second Edition, Genitourinary Imaging — “Scrotum and testicle,” GU pages 285 and 291–292 (PDF pages 297, 303–304) was reviewed. Core confirms that:

- A spermatocele is a sperm-containing cystic dilation of the epididymis, usually in the epididymal head.
- Internal low-level mobile echoes are the classic sonographic clue.
- Ultrasound cannot reliably distinguish a simple epididymal cyst from a spermatocele.
- Epididymal obstruction may produce associated tubular ectasia of the rete testis.
- Adult extratesticular masses are usually benign, while vascularized soft tissue still requires caution.

Whole-source coverage audit completed from the full relevant Core pages and the fused RadPrimer/STATdx package. Card generation used full-source review, not the validation digest or summary field.
